fields.summary: User can reset their password via an emailed link
fields.description:
As a registered user I want to reset my password through a link sent to my email so that I can regain access when I forget it.

Project Key: SMOKE
Issue ID (numeric): 10001

Acceptance Criteria:
1. Submitting a registered email address on the 'Forgot password' form sends an email with a single-use password-reset link that is valid for 60 minutes.
2. Opening a reset link more than 60 minutes after it was sent shows the message 'This reset link has expired' and a 'Request a new link' button.

attachments.reset-policy.md:
Password reset policy
- A reset link stays valid for 60 minutes.
- At most 3 reset requests per account per hour.

review_comments:
**Review Feedback from Testing Team**

1. Define link renewal workflow and behavior: Acceptance Criterion 2 specifies a 'Request a new link' button on the expired link page, but does not define the user action, workflow steps, or expected result when clicked (e.g., whether it automatically dispatches a new email to the associated address or redirects the user to the 'Forgot password' form).

2. Specify rate limiting behavior for requests and renewals: Incorporate the rate limiting rule from 'reset-policy.md' ("At most 3 reset requests per account per hour") into both the initial request workflow and the link renewal flow, specifying the expected UI response, error message, or system behavior when the threshold is exceeded.

3. Define handling of unregistered and invalid emails: Specify the expected system behavior and UI response when an unregistered, invalid, or inactive email address is submitted, including rules for preventing user enumeration.

4. Clarify expiration boundary conditions: Acceptance Criterion 2 states the link expires "more than 60 minutes after it was sent"; clarify the exact boundary condition to eliminate ambiguity regarding whether the link is considered valid or expired at exactly 60 minutes.

5. Specify email dispatch parameters: Define concrete email parameters required for verification and testing, including the sender address, subject line, body copy/template, and reset URL structure.

6. Define form submission feedback: Specify the explicit UI confirmation, notification, or status message displayed on the 'Forgot password' form upon submitting a request.

7. Clarify localization handling: Explain how the `locale` parameter defined in 'reset-request.json' affects the email dispatch and the selection of localized email templates.

8. Explicitly reference attachments: Reference the attachments 'reset-policy.md' and 'reset-request.json' directly within the issue description and acceptance criteria to ensure traceability.

test_cases.name: Verify password reset email is sent for registered user
test_cases.objective: Submit a registered email address on the 'Forgot password' form, verify the confirmation message and delivered email in en-GB, and confirm the reset link is valid and single-use.
test_cases.precondition: The user has a registered account with email 'user@example.com' and the 'Forgot password' page is open.
test_cases.review_comments:
Test case review

Review iterations: 2, stop reason: iteration_limit.

  • [HIGH] imprecise expected result (AC-1): Step 4 has the weakest expected result in the test case: stating that 'An error message is displayed indicating that the reset link has already been used or is invalid, confirming the link is single-use and cannot be reused' is underspecified. It leaves the exact expected UI error state, message text, and redirection behavior undefined, which can lead testers to evaluate the test outcome inconsistently. Additionally, the action uses tentative wording ('Attempt to open').
    Suggested fix: Refine step 4 by changing the action to 'Open the same password-reset link from step 1 in the web browser.' and making the expected result precise by specifying the exact error message text, page state, and available user actions (such as a 'Request a new link' button).
  • [HIGH] imprecise expected result (AC-1): Step 3 expected result is underspecified by stating only that 'A confirmation message is displayed indicating that the password has been reset successfully.' It omits the exact confirmation message text and fails to define the subsequent navigation state (such as redirection to the login page or presenting a 'Log in' button), leaving testers to evaluate the post-reset outcome inconsistently.
    Suggested fix: Specify the exact confirmation message text (e.g. 'Your password has been successfully reset.') and define the post-submission UI state (e.g. redirection to the login page with a login form displayed).
  • [MEDIUM] test data in expected results (AC-1): Step 1 expected results directly duplicate test data values ('en-GB' and 'user@example.com') instead of referencing them, violating the rule that test data must appear only in the test data field.
    Suggested fix: Update Step 1 expected results to refer to the test data rather than duplicating it (e.g. replace 'user@example.com' with 'the specified email address' and 'en-GB' with 'the specified locale').
  • [MEDIUM] duplicate step (AC-1): Step 2 partially duplicates existing test case SMOKE-T101, which already verifies that opening the received password-reset link navigates to and displays the password reset form.
    Suggested fix: Remove the standalone verification in Step 2 that duplicates SMOKE-T101, combining navigation to the reset form directly into Step 3 where the new password is submitted.

Duplicate check

This test case overlaps in coverage with:

  • SMOKE-T101: Both test cases verify that opening the password-reset link received in the email navigates to and displays the password reset form.

test_cases.name: Verify expired password reset link behavior
test_cases.objective: Open a password-reset link more than 60 minutes after generation and verify the expiration message and 'Request a new link' button are displayed.
test_cases.precondition: A password-reset link sent 61 minutes ago to 'user@example.com' is available.
test_cases.review_comments:
Test case review

Review iterations: 2, stop reason: iteration_limit.

  • [HIGH] missing step (2): Step 1 expected results state that the 'Request a new link' button 'links to the Forgot password page', but Step 1 only opens the reset link in a browser without clicking the button. Verifying that the button navigates to the 'Forgot password' page requires an interaction, leaving the expected result unverifiable from the current action alone and causing testers to execute or skip this verification inconsistently.
    Suggested fix: Update Step 1 expected results to verify that the expiration message, no password input fields, and the 'Request a new link' button are displayed. Add Step 2 with action 'Click the 'Request a new link' button.' and expected result 'The 'Forgot password' page is displayed.'
  • [HIGH] imprecise test data (AC-2): Step 1 test data specifies a static mock URL with a placeholder token ('https://example.com/reset-password?token=expired-token-61m') rather than defining valid test data that exercises the actual 60-minute token expiration logic. In a real test environment, an arbitrary token string will fail on token validation/malformation rather than verifying AC-2 expiration behavior.
    Suggested fix: Update the test data to specify a genuinely generated reset token whose timestamp is 61 minutes in the past (e.g. created via API or system time offset) to properly exercise link expiration logic.

Duplicate check

No duplicate test cases found.

steps.description: Open the reset link in a web browser.
steps.expected_result: The message 'This reset link has expired' is displayed, no password input fields are shown, and the 'Request a new link' button is displayed, enabled, and links to the 'Forgot password' page.

test_cases.name: Verify rate limiting for password reset requests
test_cases.objective: Submit 3 password-reset requests for a registered account within one hour and verify each succeeds, then attempt a 4th request within the same window and verify it is rate-limited.
test_cases.precondition: The user has a registered account with email 'user@example.com' with no reset requests made in the past 60 minutes, and the 'Forgot password' page is open.
test_cases.review_comments:
Test case review

Review iterations: 2, stop reason: iteration_limit.

  • [HIGH] imprecise expected result: In Step 2, the expected result states 'The request is blocked or throttled with an appropriate rate-limit error message displayed, and no password-reset email is sent.' Describing the outcome with ambiguous alternatives ('blocked or throttled') and an unspecified ('appropriate') error message leaves the verification criteria open to interpretation. Testers cannot consistently verify whether the application handled rate-limiting correctly or missed a defect in user messaging.
    Suggested fix: Specify the precise rate-limiting UI outcome and exact error message text (e.g. 'A rate-limit warning message stating \"You have reached the maximum number of reset attempts allowed per hour. Please try again later.\" is displayed, and no password-reset email is sent.').
  • [HIGH] imprecise expected result: Step 1 expected results state that 'confirmation messages are displayed, and a password-reset email is sent for each request' without specifying the exact confirmation message text or validating that each delivered email contains a distinct, unique reset link and the required 60-minute expiration notice from reset-policy.md. Testers could overlook defects if duplicate reset links or incorrect messages are generated.
    Suggested fix: Specify the exact confirmation message text displayed after each submission and explicitly verify that three separate emails are received, each containing a distinct reset link with explicit 60-minute validity text.
  • [MEDIUM] test data in action: The actions in Step 1 and Step 2 hardcode test data values ('3 consecutive times within a one-hour window' and '4th password-reset request within the same one-hour window') rather than referencing the values defined in the test data field.
    Suggested fix: Rephrase the actions to reference the test data fields (e.g. Step 1: 'Enter the registered email address and submit the 'Forgot password' form for the specified number of requests within the specified timeframe.', Step 2: 'Enter the registered email address and submit the form for the next request attempt within the same timeframe.').

Duplicate check

No duplicate test cases found.

steps.description: Enter the registered email address and submit the 'Forgot password' form 3 consecutive times within a one-hour window.
steps.expected_result: Each of the 3 requests is processed successfully, confirmation messages are displayed, and a password-reset email is sent for each request.
steps.test_data:
email: user@example.com
number of requests: 3
timeframe: within 60 minutes

steps.description: Enter the same registered email address and submit a 4th password-reset request within the same one-hour window.
steps.expected_result: The request is blocked or throttled with an appropriate rate-limit error message displayed, and no password-reset email is sent.

bugs.summary: [Password Reset] - POST /api/password-reset returns HTTP 500 Internal Server Error
bugs.description:
Description:
During execution of test case 'Password reset email is sent for a registered address' (SMOKE-T100), sending a password reset request to /api/password-reset failed with HTTP 500 Internal Server Error instead of the expected HTTP 200. No reset email was queued.

Error:
AssertionError: expected response status 200 but received 500

Environment Details:
- Agent: Smoke API Test Executor (version 9.9-smoke)
- Environment: Smoke Test Environment

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Ensure a user account exists for the test email address (registered@example.com).
2. Send POST /api/password-reset with the registered email address (email=registered@example.com).

Expected Result:
HTTP 200 and a password-reset email is queued.

Actual Result:
HTTP 500 Internal Server Error; no email was queued.
